plain: John Mack, head of the psychiatry department at Harvard, is said to have spent the last part of his career studying people who said aliens had abducted them, and in the 1990s he used hypnotic regression and holotropic breathwork, a method of deep, rapid breathing, to bring back his patients' memories of being taken. Michels tells this on several episodes and sometimes adds that Mack was friends with Thomas Kuhn, the philosopher of science who wrote The Structure of Scientific Revolutions, though one telling leaves Kuhn out. The point is that a senior Harvard psychiatrist took abduction accounts seriously.
